sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Kubernetes interview questions are now standard for any senior Java backend role — pods, deployments, services, ingress, ConfigMaps and Secrets, HPA and resource requests/limits, StatefulSets and persistent volumes, rolling updates and rollback, network policies, RBAC, and the production-debugging questions interviewers ask ("a pod is in CrashLoopBackOff — walk me through your debug"). Pair this page with the Docker, CI/CD and Cloud-Native pages for the full container-platform interview surface.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
K8s = **control loops over a desired-state spec**.

- **Pod** is the atom; **Deployment** owns replica sets.
- **Service** = stable virtual IP; **Ingress** = HTTP routing.
- **ConfigMap / Secret** for config; **PVC** for storage.
- **Probes** — liveness restarts the pod, readiness gates traffic.
- **HPA / VPA** — scale on CPU / memory / custom metrics.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Helm** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Kubernetes configuration** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Kubernetes fundamentals** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Kubernetes networking** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Kubernetes scaling** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Kubernetes workloads** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **CrashLoopBackOff** debug — `kubectl describe` for events, `logs --previous` for the prior crash.
- **Resource requests + limits** — requests reserve, limits cap; OOMKilled if you hit memory limit.
- **StatefulSet vs Deployment** — stable identity + ordered start; for databases, kafka.
- **Network policies** — deny by default, allow per-namespace.
- **Helm vs Kustomize** — templates vs overlays; both fine, pick one.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd deploy stateless apps as a Deployment with readiness + liveness probes, set realistic requests/limits, expose via Service + Ingress, manage config in ConfigMap / Secrets, and scale with HPA on a metric that tracks user-perceived load."*
